page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.32-256 is an enterprise virtual machine built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration is powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors operating at a fixed frequency of 3.6 GHz. It allocates 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading overhead. Memory is provisioned at 256.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance contains no integrated local storage, requiring persistent operational data and operating system installations to rely entirely on external block storage volumes. Accelerator hardware is not included, with zero GPUs present on the host. Network access includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for inbound and outbound routing.

With dedicated physical cores eliminating thread-contention issues, the instance offers predictable processing throughput across high-concurrency tasks. The balanced 4.0 GB per core resource distribution aligns well with containerized microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed data processing, and large-scale web application serving optimized for the Arm64 instruction set.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.32-256 is an Arm-based virtual machine engineered for general-purpose workloads. Driven by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor running at 3.6 GHz, this configuration supplies 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a single execution thread per core, avoiding resource contention associated with hyperthreading. The server provides 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, making storage persistence reliant on remote block volumes. The system includes zero GPU accelerators and provides one complimentary public IPv4 address. The balanced compute-to-memory density makes this instance suitable for container clusters, scale-out web serving, build automation, and distributed batch processing workloads built for 64-bit Arm architectures.
